hypotheses.justification: The finiteness of the index type is never needed for the truth of the statement: when ι is not finite the remaining hypotheses are contradictory, so the disjunction holds vacuously. Indeed, by `hs`, `s^[n] = id` with `n` prime (so `n ≥ 2`), hence `s` is a bijective ring endomorphism of `R`: `s ∘ s^[n-1] = id` and `s^[n-1] ∘ s = id`. Transporting along `φ`, `t := conj φ s` is a ring automorphism of `Π i, F i` with `t^[n] = id`. A ring automorphism preserves idempotents and the partial order on them, hence preserves atoms; the atoms of `Π i, F i` (each `F i` a field) are exactly the elements `ind {i}`: an idempotent `u` satisfies `u * ind {i} = u` iff `u = 0` or `u = ind {i}`. So `t (ind {i}) = ind {σ i}` for a permutation `σ` of `ι`, and `t^[n] = id` gives `σ^[n] = id`, so every `σ`-orbit has size `1` or `n`. If `σ ≠ id` there is an orbit `O` with `#O = n ≥ 2`; since `ι` is infinite, `O ≠ ∅` and `O ≠ univ`, and `ind O` is a fixed idempotent of `t` (as `σ O = O`) which is neither `0` nor `1`. If `σ = id`, then every `ind {i}` is fixed, and again (as `ι` is infinite, `ind {i} ≠ 0, 1`) we get a fixed idempotent other than `0, 1`. In either case `φ.symm (ind O)` (resp. `φ.symm (ind {i})`) is an idempotent fixed by `s` which is not `0` or `1`, contradicting `hfix`: any element of `Set.range f` that is idempotent is of the form `f x` with `x` idempotent in the field `k`, so `x = 0` or `1` and the element is `0` or `1` (this is exactly the argument used for `hfix01` in the existing proof, which does not use finiteness). Hence for infinite `ι` the hypotheses are unsatisfiable and the theorem still holds after deleting `[Finite ι]`; the proof only has to split on `Finite ι` and handle the infinite case by this contradiction (e.g. by importing `Finite.of_injective`/`Set.Infinite` facts, or by producing a nonempty proper `σ`-orbit as above), while the finite case is the existing proof. No other hypothesis can be deleted: for instance `hn` is essential, since for `n = 0`, `R = k × k`, `ι = Bool`, `s` the swap and `f : k →+* k × k` the diagonal map, all hypotheses except `hn` hold (`hs` is trivial and the fixed points of `s` are precisely the range of `f`), yet the first disjunct would require `0 = 1` and `k × k` is not a field; `hfix` and `φ` are likewise needed (e.g. `R = k[ε]/(ε²)` with `s(ε) = -ε`, `n = 2`, shows `φ` cannot be dropped).
